title: ape-pods: develop and run Pods against the real database
goal: Provide the four requested ape-pods commands as a standalone Node CLI against the real selected database, with Pod identity, configured owner/isolated home and shared-data permissions.
summary: The CLI is standalone for this increment: no desktop attachment, desktop protocol upgrade or Electron build/install/start is required. It reuses the execution core and real selected database, retains identity/home/shared-data behavior and refuses an active desktop profile. Extra application-secret management and storage migration remain excluded.

problem.statement: The existing runner can execute in Node tests, but product initialization and privileged services still depend on Electron.
problem.impact: There is no supported terminal workflow to manage real Pods and run them without launching the desktop.
problem.approach: Add a thin CLI, a runtime-only build and shared host adapters while retaining the real database, resources and authorization checks.
problem.outcome: The same Pod IDs and edits appear in CLI and desktop, and a foreground run returns a durable result without packaging or launching Electron.

context: The owner requested four commands, metadata editing including tags, and the real database. The owner then excluded credential support and clarified that the Pod must still execute under its identity and the owner or Pod home context. Revision 3 therefore excludes additional application-secret management while retaining existing identity authentication, grants and configured execution context. The source baseline is main 2d24afe92c3dc3f994ba626c93e725ea90ac01b0. Unrelated untracked work is preserved. The command scope is authorized; this newly authored implementation plan is awaiting approval. Revision 4 adds the owner requirement to retain current shared-storage access. The owner also stated that every Pod should function alone and solve one very small task, with a future move toward Pod-owned storage. This is future architecture direction; shared-storage replacement is not part of the current implementation. After approving revision 4, the owner explicitly narrowed the implementation: "Lass den Desktop mal Desktop sein. Cli einfach separat inzwischen." This instruction removes desktop attachment and upgrade coordination; revision 5 records that condition under the existing implementation authorization. Worktree base is canonical main b46051395a10b010b933efde9f71665d0c11a9d8.
scope: Use the real selected desktop profile by default, including selected-profile.json; --profile PATH explicitly selects another real profile. Never silently copy or replace the owner database. Automated tests use disposable databases with the production schema.

Expose exactly the four requested commands with --help and --json. create and edit accept terminal input only when interactive; explicit flags support automation. edit ID changes name, tags and supported lifecycle metadata through existing revision checks; optional --script imports the canonical pod-script.mjs through the existing validation and activation flow.

A run uses the active validated script, original Pod identity, existing runtime and exact-command grants, configured home context, checkpoints and durable history. owner uses the OS owner home for the existing owner-context boundaries; isolated uses the Pod home and scoped resources. Never inherit the invoking terminal environment blindly or substitute owner identity for Pod identity. Additional application-secret injection is unsupported and fails explicitly.

Reuse the same runtime/command producers through a shared host seam. Provide a runtime-only build and local ape-pods executable. Do not add desktop CLI channels, attach to a running desktop or require a new signed desktop installation.

Retain existing shared domain-data access, namespaces, reader/writer permissions, revision checks and work-claim semantics through the same runtime APIs. A CLI run uses its Pod ID and run ID as data principal; owner home never grants owner-level access to all shared data. No parallel data store is created.
nonGoals: A permanent daemon, automatic CLI scheduling, cross-platform execution, full desktop replacement and npm or signed desktop releases are outside this increment.

New application credential CRUD, assigned-secret import or injection, new login flows and credential-format migration are outside version 1. Existing Pod identity material and identity/grant services may be consumed as required for a real run; existing owner-home application logins may be used under the configured owner policy. No plaintext replacement, owner-login mutation or permission bypass is introduced.
Do not run, edit or migrate existing owner Pods as acceptance fixtures, change owner login files, or ship a reduced mock executor as a successful real run.

Replacing shared storage with Pod-owned storage, migrating domain data or redesigning Pod collaboration is outside this CLI increment. Treat each Pod as one small independently executable responsibility and avoid new hidden coupling. No separate physical database per Pod is decided by this proposal.

sections.title: Command behavior
sections.body:
`ape-pods list [--json]` shows IDs, names, tags, lifecycle and last run status.

`ape-pods run <id> [--json]` executes the active script once and waits; human progress goes to stderr, structured output to stdout. Exit codes distinguish success, failed/blocked runs, invalid input, unavailable runtime and cancellation. Unknown external effects retain the existing recovery state and are never automatically replayed.

`ape-pods create [--name NAME] [--tags a,b] [--script pod-script.mjs]` creates a paused Pod in the selected real profile. A script is saved, prepared, validated and activated through current commands; a validation error leaves the Pod paused and reports its ID and draft state.

`ape-pods edit [<id>] [--name NAME] [--tags a,b] [--lifecycle active|paused|archived] [--script pod-script.mjs]` edits metadata and optionally replaces the script through the same flow. No-ID selection and field prompts are TTY-only; automation must provide an ID and changes. Clearing tags is explicit. A stale revision is rejected. Failed script validation preserves the previous active version. Editing lifecycle may affect the existing desktop scheduler; the CLI host does not start a scheduler.

sections.title: Repository orientation and architecture
sections.body:
Keep the CLI entry in apps/openape-pods/src/cli and reuse the existing worker and RunDispatcher. Extract the current host implementation once into src/main/runtime-worker.ts; the existing Electron wrapper retains its default behavior, while Node supplies process transport, paths and identity-cipher access. This source extraction adds no desktop integration feature and requires no desktop build for CLI use.

Node forks the existing worker entry over IPC. PODS_ONESHOT disables scheduler intake and starts only the explicit manual run. The worker holds an OS profile lease through child cleanup and storage close, preventing concurrent standalone CLI workers. Before starting and before each command, check the existing desktop SingletonLock and refuse an active owner. Desktop and CLI are not supported concurrently; the owner must keep desktop closed for the full command. No claim is made that the installed desktop participates in the new CLI lease.

The CLI uses the real selected profile and existing command validators. Shared state, script validation, checkpoints, recovery and Pod authorization remain common. Extract reusable asset preparation from the existing build recipe, and compile the CLI/worker/native helpers without Electron main/preload or Vite renderer output.

sections.title: Pod identity and home context remain mandatory
sections.body:
Pod identity and home context are independent. The DDISA principal remains the selected Pod and the existing owner binding and runtime/exact-command grants are verified. owner does not mean authorizing every request as the human owner. OS processes continue to use the supported local OS user and sandbox; no new OS-user switching is introduced.

Read the stored sandbox level instead of selecting a context from the CLI environment. At owner-context boundaries, HOME resolves to the owner home, including its existing application settings and logins where policy permits. At isolated boundaries, HOME resolves to the Pod home; do not copy or mount owner login stores into it. Preserve the workspace, Pod ID, scoped PATH, environment allowlist, denylist and protected profile/control-socket/owner-apes-login paths. Test the actual top-level script and spawned application boundaries separately: the current runner passes a Pod home while programHome applies owner versus isolated reach to program execution. Match desktop semantics explicitly instead of claiming that every existing script already receives owner HOME. If the requested top-level context requires a behavior change, document and verify that change with the shared producer; never expand filesystem reach silently.

The exclusion of credentials applies to new application-secret management and injection. Existing Pod identity keys, tokens, grant checks and owner-home application logins remain usable through current services. The Node host may require a minimal adapter to read existing identity material safely; prove compatibility, locked-store refusal and unchanged owner login without migrating owner data. Missing identity or revoked authority fails before script execution. No mock identity, fixture grant or host-environment fallback is allowed. list/create/edit remain independent of run credential initialization.

The CLI is standalone for now. A live desktop profile is refused; do not add a desktop socket protocol or upgrade prerequisite. Coordinate source overlap with existing host changes without implementing a separate consolidation proposal.

sections.title: Setup and delivery
sections.body:
After plan approval create a canonical native development issue, inspect current origin/main and worktrees, and implement in a dedicated feature/issue-N-ape-pods-cli worktree. Preserve all existing checkouts. Activate the pinned toolchain in every shell with `. ./scripts/activate-node.sh`, then `pnpm run doctor`. Use the existing workspace and established tests; retain current automatic and manual check selection.

During implementation use focused existing test files first, build consumed packages serially, build the changed runtime and execute the four CLI commands against an isolated production-schema fixture. Run the complete affected unit gate once at handoff or through the mandatory pre-push hook. Add the recommended create/edit/run development workflow to the Pods documentation, update active-work.md and any generated workspace/script maps, then open a native PR with an explicit issue relation. Publish actual output in a private Test Runs report. No merge, release, installation or owner-profile migration is implied by this plan.

sections.title: Current shared data and future Pod-owned state
sections.body:
Current increment: run uses the existing data and work APIs in the selected real profile. Reuse DomainData, WorkLedger and the runtime data-operation boundary. Preserve namespace reader/writer checks, schema validation, expected revisions, writer epochs, claim ownership, checkpoints and restart durability. A Pod running with owner HOME still accesses shared data as that Pod, not as the owner administrator. Deny unassigned namespaces and foreign claims, and keep existing unknown-effect handling.

Future direction from the owner: every Pod should function alone and solve one very small task; state should eventually be owned by that Pod. Keep new CLI code behind the existing data-operation boundary, without creating a second store abstraction for a future backend. Do not make a command implicitly launch sibling Pods or require a whole Pod network to run. External inputs and outputs may need a separate explicit contract when the storage redesign is planned. Backend layout, migration and data-exchange mechanics remain undecided; this CLI implementation does not replace shared storage.

milestones.title: Prove real-profile access and exclusive runtime ownership
milestones.goal: Resolve the risky host boundaries before product implementation expands.
steps: Create the native issue and isolated feature worktree after approval; freeze the reviewed baseline and inspect the existing ape-shell overlap.

Prototype standalone Node transport, runtime paths and CLI profile leasing with real-schema fixtures. Prove Pod identity and both home contexts; metadata commands must not initialize run authentication.
acceptance: A normal Node process boots the unchanged execution core without an Electron process or a second database copy.
Two standalone CLI starts produce exactly one profile owner. An active desktop lock is refused without modifying it. Concurrent desktop/CLI operation is unsupported and documented.

Existing Pod identity material can be consumed securely without credential-format migration or owner-login changes. Missing or revoked identity is refused; list/create/edit do not initialize run identity or application-secret services.
milestones.rollback: Revert the isolated feature changes; preserve owner data and use the previous desktop runtime. No automatic profile migration is part of rollback.

milestones.title: Implement list, create and metadata editing
milestones.goal: Make the four-command interface useful with the real selected profile.
steps: Add the CLI parser, profile discovery, shared command client and human/JSON output. Route list/create/edit through the existing command validators and revision handling.
Support name, tags and lifecycle updates; optional script import uses draft, dependency preparation, validation and activation from the canonical script file.
acceptance: list displays the same IDs and metadata as the selected profile in desktop.
create returns a durable paused Pod; edit changes only requested fields, supports clearing tags and rejects stale revisions.
The commands have meaningful TTY and non-TTY behavior, deterministic JSON output and tested failure exits.
milestones.rollback: Revert the isolated feature changes; preserve owner data and use the previous desktop runtime. No automatic profile migration is part of rollback.

milestones.title: Implement the real one-shot run and runtime-only build
milestones.goal: Run an existing Pod under its real identity and configured owner or isolated home context without additional application-secret support.
steps: Reuse existing Pod identity and runtime authorization, resolve the stored home/sandbox context and start only the requested run through the existing worker. Use a standalone Node host under the CLI profile lease, with desktop closed.
Prepare runtime assets without main/preload/renderer packaging, stream bounded events, wait for the terminal run state and close children and storage on exit or cancellation.

Connect the existing runtime data/work operations to the selected real database under the selected Pod identity. Preserve namespace permissions and transaction/recovery behavior; start no sibling Pod.
acceptance: A real native sandbox run preserves Pod identity, owner binding, grants, configured owner/isolated context, checkpoint and history without Electron. Tests observe HOME, working directory, scoped environment and the identity used for authorization at script and child-program boundaries.

Invalid scripts, missing or revoked identity, incompatible profiles and unsupported assigned-secret operations fail explicitly. The CLI never substitutes owner identity, a fixture grant, an arbitrary HOME or a synthetic provider.
Ctrl+C, crash recovery and unknown effects preserve existing recovery semantics; unrelated schedules never start in the CLI host.

A CLI run reads and writes authorized shared data, rejects an unassigned namespace and a foreign work claim, and preserves records/results after reopen. These checks pass in both home contexts without owner-administrator data privileges or another Pod running.
milestones.rollback: Revert the isolated feature changes; preserve owner data and use the previous desktop runtime. No automatic profile migration is part of rollback.

milestones.title: Verify and document the development workflow
milestones.goal: Deliver a reviewable native PR and actual CLI evidence.
steps: Run focused CLI/store/host tests, runtime build, real native fixture acceptance and the required affected unit gate. Exercise desktop adapter compatibility where changed.

Document local ape-pods installation and the recommended list/create/edit/run workflow. Publish a private Test Runs report, update this plan and active-work.md and open a native PR related to the issue.
acceptance: All four commands pass a create/edit/run/reopen journey against the real database engine and production schema.

Actual logs and process evidence distinguish real local execution from synthetic external services and show no Electron build, package, notary, install or launch requirement for the development cycle.
The native PR, maintained plan and verified Test Runs document state the source SHA, remaining compatibility requirements and next action.

decisions.title: Four commands and the real database
decisions.description: Use ape-pods list/run/create/edit; edit includes tags and metadata and all commands refer to real Pod records.
decisions.reference: Chat: "Passt, wir machen das jetzt. Wir brauchen ape-pods list / ape-pods run <id> / ape-pods create / ape-pods edit"; clarification: "Edit ist zum ändern von Tags usw. Wir sollten die echte Datenbank nutzen". This approves the requested scope, not an unseen implementation plan.

decisions.title: One shared execution implementation
decisions.description: Reuse existing contracts, dispatcher and privileged services through host adapters. Per the subsequent owner instruction, the CLI runs separately with desktop closed; desktop attachment and update coordination are excluded.
decisions.reference: Owner approved implementation of revision 4, then instructed: "Lass den Desktop mal Desktop sein. Cli einfach separat inzwischen."

decisions.title: Exclude additional application-secret management
decisions.description: No new application credential CRUD or assigned-secret import/injection. Existing identity authentication and grants remain mandatory; the owner clarification explicitly requires the configured owner or Pod home context.
decisions.reference: Chat: "Ich denke wir brauchen noch leinenes credentials in dieser Version." Interpreted in context as no credentials in this version; this narrows the requested scope and does not approve an unseen plan revision. Follow-up clarification: "Wichtig ist trotzdem dass der pod unter der Identität, im home context des owners oder pods ausgeführt wird".

decisions.title: Preserve identity and configured home context
decisions.description: Pod identity and runtime grants are required independently of owner versus isolated HOME. Existing identity material may be consumed; missing identity is an error, never a fallback to the CLI owner.
decisions.reference: Chat: "Wichtig ist trotzdem dass der pod unter der Identität, im home context des owners oder pods ausgeführt wird". This is a scope clarification, not approval of the full unseen implementation plan.

decisions.title: Keep shared data now; favor independent single-purpose Pods
decisions.description: This CLI version retains existing shared-storage access under Pod permissions. Future architecture should give each Pod its own state and one very small independently executable responsibility; storage replacement is a separate proposal.
decisions.reference: Chat: "Der Zugriff auf den gemeinsamen Speicher brauchen wir wohl auch noch, obwohl ich den gerne in Zukunft gegen einen pod eigenen Speicher auflösen möchte. Ich finde jeder pod muss für sich ganz alleine funktionieren. Jeder pod löst eine ganz kleine Aufgabe". This sets current scope and future direction, not migration approval.

risks.title: Concurrent use of the same profile
risks.mitigation: CLI workers share an OS lease and refuse an active desktop SingletonLock. Desktop must remain closed while a CLI command runs; no desktop protocol or update is added. Preserve data and fail before opening mutable storage when another owner is detected.

risks.title: Real profile implies real side effects
risks.mitigation: Run uses the same grants and exact-call checks as desktop. Automated verification uses disposable production-schema fixtures; real-profile acceptance is read-only list unless an exact further action is authorized. Preserve unknown-effect recovery and do not retry automatically.

risks.title: Hidden Electron dependencies and concurrent host work
risks.mitigation: Trace transitive imports, prove the Node binary runs without Electron imports, and keep extraction narrow. Reconcile changes with the active ape-shell worktree instead of copying its unmerged implementation or changing its scope.

verification: CLI argument and output tests cover list/create/edit/run, non-TTY errors, JSON separation, explicit tag clearing and stale revisions using real PodDatabase stores.

Native Node acceptance creates a Pod, edits tags, runs the active script, reopens the same database and verifies identity, metadata, events, checkpoint and result. The process tree contains Node and the native helper, with no Electron launch or package/notary/install step.

Cover competing profile owners, startup races, wrong or revoked Pod identity, owner/isolated HOME and working directory, hostile caller environment, protected paths, unsupported assigned-secret calls, Ctrl+C and crash recovery. Identity access is scoped to existing runtime needs; isolated execution never copies owner login stores.

Retain focused desktop host and worker-entry coverage, runtime build and the affected unit gate. Publish source SHA, exact commands and actual identity/context evidence. Isolated fixtures can test identity compatibility; do not unlock or mutate the real owner keychain or run owner Pods as fixtures. Distinguish protocol fixtures from live-provider acceptance.

Use real shared-data tables and runtime operations in disposable production-schema fixtures: allowed reader/writer, refused namespace, stale expected revision, claim ownership and durable result after restart. Verify that owner HOME never switches the data principal to owner, and that only the requested Pod starts.
handoff: Implementation and focused acceptance are complete in feature/issue-1499-ape-pods-cli. Runtime-only build, 33 focused cases, four native Node CLI cases and generated documentation checks pass. The required affected unit gate, publication of actual evidence and native PR handoff are next. Desktop remains separate and must stay closed during a CLI command.

completion.summary: Implementation is complete; final affected checks and review handoff are pending. No release, merge or desktop installation is part of this task.

changelog.text: Created revision 1 after the owner clarified metadata editing and use of the real database. Recorded the previously underestimated host extraction and installed-profile compatibility work.
Revision 2 removes credential compatibility, keychain integration and secret/login support at the owner request. The real database, four commands and exclusive profile ownership remain in scope.

Revision 3 corrects the overly broad credential exclusion after the owner required real Pod identity and owner/Pod home context. Existing identity authentication is mandatory; only additional application-secret management remains excluded. Source inspection distinguishes top-level script HOME from programHome.

Revision 4 adds explicit shared-domain-data and work access with Pod-scoped authorization. Records the owner direction of small independent Pods with Pod-owned state, while keeping storage replacement outside this implementation.
Patrick approved revision 4 in the chat: "Passt. Setze das cli um". Started implementation from current canonical main; no owner Pod has been modified.
Revision 5 records the owner instruction to keep the CLI standalone for now. Removed desktop attachment and upgrade coordination; require desktop closed and share an OS lease between CLI workers.

Exit codes distinguish success, failed/blocked runs, invalid input, unavailable runtime and cancellation. Unknown external effects retain the existing recovery state and are never automatically replayed.

`ape-pods create [--name NAME] [--tags a,b] [--script pod-script.mjs]` creates a paused Pod in the selected real profile. A script is saved, prepared, validated and activated through current commands; a validation error leaves the Pod paused and reports its ID and draft state.

`ape-pods edit [<id>] [--name NAME] [--tags a,b] [--lifecycle active|paused|archived] [--script pod-script.mjs]` edits metadata and optionally replaces the script through the same flow. No-ID selection and field prompts are TTY-only; automation must provide an ID and changes. Clearing tags is explicit. A stale revision is rejected. Failed script validation preserves the previous active version. Editing lifecycle may affect the existing desktop scheduler; the CLI host does not start a scheduler.
entries.text:
`ape-pods list [--json]` zeigt IDs, Namen, Tags, Lebenszyklus und den letzten Laufstatus.

`ape-pods run <id> [--json]` führt das aktive Skript einmal aus und wartet; lesbarer Fortschritt geht an stderr, strukturierte Ausgabe an stdout. Exitcodes unterscheiden Erfolg, fehlgeschlagene/blockierte Läufe, ungültige Eingaben, nicht verfügbare Runtime und Abbruch. Unklare externe Effekte behalten den bestehenden Recovery-Status und werden niemals automatisch wiederholt.

`ape-pods create [--name NAME] [--tags a,b] [--script pod-script.mjs]` erstellt einen pausierten Pod im ausgewählten echten Profil. Ein Skript wird über die bestehenden Befehle gespeichert, vorbereitet, validiert und aktiviert; bei Validierungsfehlern bleibt der Pod pausiert und ID sowie Entwurfsstatus werden ausgegeben.

`ape-pods edit [<id>] [--name NAME] [--tags a,b] [--lifecycle active|paused|archived] [--script pod-script.mjs]` ändert Metadaten und optional das Skript über denselben Ablauf. Auswahl ohne ID und Feldabfragen sind nur mit TTY möglich; Automatisierung muss ID und Änderungen angeben. Das Leeren von Tags ist ausdrücklich. Veraltete Revisionen werden abgelehnt. Fehlgeschlagene Skriptvalidierung erhält die vorherige aktive Version. Lebenszyklusänderungen können den bestehenden Desktop-Scheduler beeinflussen; der CLI-Host startet keinen Scheduler.

entries.source: Repository orientation and architecture
entries.text: Repository-Orientierung und Architektur

entries.source:
Keep the CLI entry in apps/openape-pods/src/cli and reuse the existing worker and RunDispatcher. Extract the current host implementation once into src/main/runtime-worker.ts; the existing Electron wrapper retains its default behavior, while Node supplies process transport, paths and identity-cipher access. This source extraction adds no desktop integration feature and requires no desktop build for CLI use.

Node forks the existing worker entry over IPC. PODS_ONESHOT disables scheduler intake and starts only the explicit manual run. The worker holds an OS profile lease through child cleanup and storage close, preventing concurrent standalone CLI workers. Before starting and before each command, check the existing desktop SingletonLock and refuse an active owner. Desktop and CLI are not supported concurrently; the owner must keep desktop closed for the full command. No claim is made that the installed desktop participates in the new CLI lease.

The CLI uses the real selected profile and existing command validators. Shared state, script validation, checkpoints, recovery and Pod authorization remain common. Extract reusable asset preparation from the existing build recipe, and compile the CLI/worker/native helpers without Electron main/preload or Vite renderer output.
entries.text:
CLI-Einstieg unter apps/openape-pods/src/cli halten und bestehenden Worker sowie RunDispatcher wiederverwenden. Die aktuelle Host-Implementierung einmal nach src/main/runtime-worker.ts herauslösen; der vorhandene Electron-Wrapper behält sein Standardverhalten, während Node Prozesstransport, Pfade und Identitäts-Cipher-Zugriff bereitstellt. Diese Quellcode-Extraktion ergänzt keine Desktop-Integrationsfunktion und benötigt für die CLI keinen Desktop-Build.

Node startet den bestehenden Worker-Einstieg über IPC. PODS_ONESHOT deaktiviert Scheduler-Intake und startet ausschließlich den ausdrücklich angeforderten manuellen Lauf. Der Worker hält eine Betriebssystem-Profilsperre bis nach Kindprozessbereinigung und Datenbankabschluss; dadurch werden parallele eigenständige CLI-Worker verhindert. Vor dem Start und vor jedem Befehl die bestehende Desktop-SingletonLock prüfen und einen aktiven Verantwortlichen ablehnen. Desktop und CLI werden nicht gleichzeitig unterstützt; der Eigentümer muss den Desktop während des gesamten Befehls geschlossen halten. Es wird nicht behauptet, dass der installierte Desktop an der neuen CLI-Sperre teilnimmt.

Die CLI verwendet echtes ausgewähltes Profil und bestehende Befehlsvalidatoren. Gemeinsame Daten, Skriptvalidierung, Checkpoints, Recovery und Pod-Berechtigungen bleiben gemeinsam implementiert. Wiederverwendbare Artefaktvorbereitung aus dem bestehenden Build-Rezept herauslösen und CLI/Worker/native Helper ohne Electron-Main-/Preload- oder Vite-Renderer-Ausgabe bauen.

entries.source: Pod identity and home context remain mandatory
entries.text: Pod-Identität und Home-Kontext bleiben verpflichtend

entries.source:
Pod identity and home context are independent. The DDISA principal remains the selected Pod and the existing owner binding and runtime/exact-command grants are verified. owner does not mean authorizing every request as the human owner. OS processes continue to use the supported local OS user and sandbox; no new OS-user switching is introduced.

Read the stored sandbox level instead of selecting a context from the CLI environment. At owner-context boundaries, HOME resolves to the owner home, including its existing application settings and logins where policy permits. At isolated boundaries, HOME resolves to the Pod home; do not copy or mount owner login stores into it. Preserve the workspace, Pod ID, scoped PATH, environment allowlist, denylist and protected profile/control-socket/owner-apes-login paths. Test the actual top-level script and spawned application boundaries separately: the current runner passes a Pod home while programHome applies owner versus isolated reach to program execution. Match desktop semantics explicitly instead of claiming that every existing script already receives owner HOME. If the requested top-level context requires a behavior change, document and verify that change with the shared producer; never expand filesystem reach silently.

The exclusion of credentials applies to new application-secret management and injection. Existing Pod identity keys, tokens, grant checks and owner-home application logins remain usable through current services. The Node host may require a minimal adapter to read existing identity material safely; prove compatibility, locked-store refusal and unchanged owner login without migrating owner data. Missing identity or revoked authority fails before script execution. No mock identity, fixture grant or host-environment fallback is allowed. list/create/edit remain independent of run credential initialization.

The CLI is standalone for now. A live desktop profile is refused; do not add a desktop socket protocol or upgrade prerequisite. Coordinate source overlap with existing host changes without implementing a separate consolidation proposal.
entries.text:
Pod-Identität und Home-Kontext sind unabhängig. DDISA-Identität bleibt der ausgewählte Pod; bestehende Owner-Bindung sowie Runtime-/Exact-Command-Grants werden geprüft. owner bedeutet nicht, jeden Aufruf als menschlichen Eigentümer zu autorisieren. Betriebssystemprozesse verwenden weiterhin den unterstützten lokalen Betriebssystembenutzer und die Sandbox; ein neuer Wechsel von Betriebssystembenutzern wird nicht eingeführt.

Den gespeicherten Sandbox-Level lesen, statt den Kontext aus der CLI-Umgebung abzuleiten. An Owner-Kontext-Grenzen zeigt HOME auf das Owner-Home einschließlich vorhandener Anwendungs-Einstellungen und Anmeldungen, soweit die Policy dies erlaubt. An isolierten Grenzen zeigt HOME auf das Pod-Home; Eigentümer-Anmeldespeicher weder hineinkopieren noch einbinden. Workspace, Pod-ID, begrenzten PATH, Umgebungs-Allowlist, Denylist und geschützte Profil-/Steuersocket-/Eigentümer-apes-Anmeldepfade erhalten. Tatsächliches Top-Level-Skript und gestartete Anwendungen getrennt prüfen: Der aktuelle Runner übergibt ein Pod-Home, während programHome den Owner-/isolierten Zugriff für Programme anwendet. Desktop-Semantik ausdrücklich abgleichen, statt zu behaupten, dass bereits jedes Skript Owner-HOME erhält. Erfordert der gewünschte Top-Level-Kontext eine Verhaltensänderung, diese am gemeinsamen Produzenten dokumentieren und prüfen; Dateisystemzugriff niemals still ausweiten.

Der Ausschluss von Credentials bezieht sich auf neue Verwaltung und Bereitstellung von Anwendungs-Secrets. Vorhandene Pod-Identitätsschlüssel, Tokens, Grant-Prüfungen und Anwendungs-Anmeldungen im Owner-Home bleiben über bestehende Dienste nutzbar. Der Node-Host kann einen minimalen Adapter zum sicheren Lesen vorhandenen Identitätsmaterials benötigen; Kompatibilität, Ablehnung gesperrten Speichers und unveränderte Eigentümer-Anmeldung ohne Migration der Eigentümerdaten nachweisen. Fehlende Identität oder widerrufene Berechtigung scheitert vor Skriptausführung. Mock-Identität, Fixture-Grant oder Fallback auf die Host-Umgebung sind ausgeschlossen. list/create/edit bleiben unabhängig von der Credential-Initialisierung für Runs.

Die CLI ist vorerst eigenständig. Ein aktives Desktop-Profil wird abgelehnt; weder Desktop-Socket-Protokoll noch Update-Voraussetzung ergänzen. Quellcodeüberschneidungen mit bestehenden Host-Änderungen abstimmen, ohne einen separaten Konsolidierungsvorschlag umzusetzen.

entries.source: Setup and delivery
entries.text: Setup und Lieferung

entries.source:
After plan approval create a canonical native development issue, inspect current origin/main and worktrees, and implement in a dedicated feature/issue-N-ape-pods-cli worktree. Preserve all existing checkouts. Activate the pinned toolchain in every shell with `. ./scripts/activate-node.sh`, then `pnpm run doctor`. Use the existing workspace and established tests; retain current automatic and manual check selection.

During implementation use focused existing test files first, build consumed packages serially, build the changed runtime and execute the four CLI commands against an isolated production-schema fixture. Run the complete affected unit gate once at handoff or through the mandatory pre-push hook. Add the recommended create/edit/run development workflow to the Pods documentation, update active-work.md and any generated workspace/script maps, then open a native PR with an explicit issue relation. Publish actual output in a private Test Runs report. No merge, release, installation or owner-profile migration is implied by this plan.
entries.text:
Nach Planfreigabe ein kanonisches natives Entwicklungsissue anlegen, origin/main und Worktrees prüfen und in einem eigenen feature/issue-N-ape-pods-cli-Worktree umsetzen. Alle bestehenden Checkouts erhalten. In jeder Shell die gepinnte Toolchain mit `. ./scripts/activate-node.sh` aktivieren, danach `pnpm run doctor` ausführen. Den bestehenden Workspace und etablierte Tests verwenden; die aktuelle automatische und manuelle Prüfauswahl erhalten.

Während der Umsetzung zuerst gezielte bestehende Testdateien verwenden, konsumierte Packages nacheinander bauen, die geänderte Runtime bauen und alle vier CLI-Befehle gegen eine isolierte Fixture mit Produktionsschema ausführen. Den vollständigen betroffenen Unit-Gate einmal bei Übergabe oder über den verpflichtenden Pre-Push-Hook ausführen. Den empfohlenen create/edit/run-Entwicklungsablauf in der Pods-Dokumentation ergänzen, active-work.md und gegebenenfalls generierte Workspace-/Skriptübersichten aktualisieren und einen nativen PR mit ausdrücklichem Issue-Bezug erstellen. Tatsächliche Ausgaben in einem privaten Test-Runs-Bericht veröffentlichen. Dieser Plan beinhaltet weder Merge, Release, Installation noch Migration des Eigentümerprofils.

entries.source: Implementation is complete; final affected checks and review handoff are pending. No release, merge or desktop installation is part of this task.
entries.text: Die Umsetzung ist abgeschlossen; abschließende betroffene Prüfungen und Übergabe zur Durchsicht stehen noch aus. Release, Merge und Desktop-Installation gehören nicht zu diesem Auftrag.

entries.source: Created revision 1 after the owner clarified metadata editing and use of the real database. Recorded the previously underestimated host extraction and installed-profile compatibility work.
entries.text: Revision 1 nach der Klarstellung des Eigentümers zu Metadatenbearbeitung und echter Datenbank erstellt. Den zuvor unterschätzten Aufwand für Host-Entkopplung und Kompatibilität des installierten Profils festgehalten.

entries.source: Exclude additional application-secret management
entries.text: Zusätzliche Verwaltung von Anwendungs-Secrets ausschließen

entries.source: No new application credential CRUD or assigned-secret import/injection. Existing identity authentication and grants remain mandatory; the owner clarification explicitly requires the configured owner or Pod home context.
entries.text: Keine neue CRUD-Verwaltung von Anwendungs-Credentials und kein Import oder Bereitstellen zugewiesener Secrets. Bestehende Identitätsauthentifizierung und Grants bleiben verpflichtend; die Klarstellung des Eigentümers verlangt ausdrücklich den konfigurierten Owner- oder Pod-Home-Kontext.

entries.source: Revision 2 removes credential compatibility, keychain integration and secret/login support at the owner request. The real database, four commands and exclusive profile ownership remain in scope.
entries.text: Revision 2 entfernt auf Wunsch des Eigentümers Credential-Kompatibilität, Keychain-Integration sowie Secret-/Login-Support. Echte Datenbank, vier Befehle und exklusive Profilverantwortung bleiben im Umfang.

entries.source: Preserve identity and configured home context
entries.text: Identität und konfigurierten Home-Kontext erhalten

entries.source: Pod identity and runtime grants are required independently of owner versus isolated HOME. Existing identity material may be consumed; missing identity is an error, never a fallback to the CLI owner.
entries.text: Pod-Identität und Runtime-Grants sind unabhängig von Owner- oder isoliertem HOME erforderlich. Vorhandenes Identitätsmaterial darf verwendet werden; fehlende Identität ist ein Fehler und niemals ein Fallback auf den CLI-Eigentümer.

entries.source: Revision 3 corrects the overly broad credential exclusion after the owner required real Pod identity and owner/Pod home context. Existing identity authentication is mandatory; only additional application-secret management remains excluded. Source inspection distinguishes top-level script HOME from programHome.
entries.text: Revision 3 korrigiert den zu weitgehenden Credential-Ausschluss, nachdem der Eigentümer echte Pod-Identität und Owner-/Pod-Home-Kontext verlangt hat. Bestehende Identitätsauthentifizierung ist verpflichtend; nur zusätzliche Verwaltung von Anwendungs-Secrets bleibt ausgeschlossen. Die Quellcodeanalyse unterscheidet Top-Level-Skript-HOME von programHome.

entries.source: Retain existing shared domain-data access, namespaces, reader/writer permissions, revision checks and work-claim semantics through the same runtime APIs. A CLI run uses its Pod ID and run ID as data principal; owner home never grants owner-level access to all shared data. No parallel data store is created.
entries.text: Bestehenden gemeinsamen Domain-Datenzugriff, Namespaces, Leser-/Schreibrechte, Revisionsprüfungen und Work-Claim-Semantik über dieselben Runtime-APIs erhalten. Ein CLI-Lauf verwendet Pod-ID und Run-ID als Datenidentität; Owner-Home gewährt niemals Eigentümerzugriff auf alle gemeinsamen Daten. Es entsteht kein paralleler Datenspeicher.

entries.source: Replacing shared storage with Pod-owned storage, migrating domain data or redesigning Pod collaboration is outside this CLI increment. Treat each Pod as one small independently executable responsibility and avoid new hidden coupling. No separate physical database per Pod is decided by this proposal.
entries.text: Gemeinsamen Speicher durch pod-eigenen Speicher ersetzen, Domain-Daten migrieren oder Pod-Zusammenarbeit neu gestalten gehört nicht zu diesem CLI-Schritt. Jeden Pod als eine kleine eigenständig ausführbare Aufgabe behandeln und neue versteckte Kopplung vermeiden. Dieser Vorschlag legt keine separate physische Datenbank pro Pod fest.

entries.source: Current shared data and future Pod-owned state
entries.text: Aktueller gemeinsamer Speicher und künftiger Pod-eigener Zustand

entries.source:
Current increment: run uses the existing data and work APIs in the selected real profile. Reuse DomainData, WorkLedger and the runtime data-operation boundary. Preserve namespace reader/writer checks, schema validation, expected revisions, writer epochs, claim ownership, checkpoints and restart durability. A Pod running with owner HOME still accesses shared data as that Pod, not as the owner administrator. Deny unassigned namespaces and foreign claims, and keep existing unknown-effect handling.

Future direction from the owner: every Pod should function alone and solve one very small task; state should eventually be owned by that Pod. Keep new CLI code behind the existing data-operation boundary, without creating a second store abstraction for a future backend. Do not make a command implicitly launch sibling Pods or require a whole Pod network to run. External inputs and outputs may need a separate explicit contract when the storage redesign is planned. Backend layout, migration and data-exchange mechanics remain undecided; this CLI implementation does not replace shared storage.
entries.text:
Aktueller Schritt: run verwendet die bestehenden Daten- und Work-APIs im ausgewählten echten Profil. DomainData, WorkLedger und die Runtime-Grenze für Datenoperationen wiederverwenden. Namespace-Leser-/Schreibprüfungen, Schemavalidierung, erwartete Revisionen, Writer-Epochen, Claim-Verantwortung, Checkpoints und Dauerhaftigkeit nach Neustart erhalten. Ein Pod mit Owner-HOME greift weiterhin als dieser Pod auf gemeinsame Daten zu, nicht als Eigentümeradministrator. Nicht zugewiesene Namespaces und fremde Claims ablehnen und die bestehende Behandlung unklarer Effekte erhalten.

Künftige Richtung des Eigentümers: Jeder Pod soll allein funktionieren und eine sehr kleine Aufgabe lösen; Zustand soll künftig diesem Pod gehören. Neuen CLI-Code hinter der vorhandenen Grenze für Datenoperationen halten, ohne eine zweite Speicherabstraktion für einen künftigen Backend-Wechsel einzuführen. Kein Befehl startet implizit andere Pods oder benötigt ein ganzes Pod-Netzwerk zum Ausführen. Externe Eingaben und Ausgaben können bei der späteren Speicherplanung einen eigenen ausdrücklichen Vertrag benötigen. Backend-Aufteilung, Migration und Datenaustauschmechanik bleiben offen; diese CLI-Umsetzung ersetzt den gemeinsamen Speicher nicht.

entries.source: Connect the existing runtime data/work operations to the selected real database under the selected Pod identity. Preserve namespace permissions and transaction/recovery behavior; start no sibling Pod.
entries.text: Bestehende Runtime-Daten-/Work-Operationen unter der ausgewählten Pod-Identität mit der echten ausgewählten Datenbank verbinden. Namespace-Rechte sowie Transaktions-/Recovery-Verhalten erhalten; keinen anderen Pod starten.

entries.source: A CLI run reads and writes authorized shared data, rejects an unassigned namespace and a foreign work claim, and preserves records/results after reopen. These checks pass in both home contexts without owner-administrator data privileges or another Pod running.
entries.text: Ein CLI-Lauf liest und schreibt berechtigte gemeinsame Daten, lehnt einen nicht zugewiesenen Namespace sowie fremden Work-Claim ab und erhält Datensätze/Ergebnisse nach erneutem Öffnen. Diese Prüfungen bestehen in beiden Home-Kontexten ohne Datenrechte des Eigentümeradministrators und ohne weiteren laufenden Pod.

entries.source: Use real shared-data tables and runtime operations in disposable production-schema fixtures: allowed reader/writer, refused namespace, stale expected revision, claim ownership and durable result after restart. Verify that owner HOME never switches the data principal to owner, and that only the requested Pod starts.
entries.text: Echte Tabellen gemeinsamer Daten und Runtime-Operationen in wegwerfbaren Fixtures mit Produktionsschema verwenden: berechtigter Leser/Schreiber, abgelehnter Namespace, veraltete erwartete Revision, Claim-Verantwortung und dauerhaftes Ergebnis nach Neustart. Nachweisen, dass Owner-HOME die Datenidentität niemals auf owner umschaltet und ausschließlich der angeforderte Pod startet.

entries.source: Keep shared data now; favor independent single-purpose Pods
entries.text: Gemeinsamen Speicher erhalten; eigenständige Pods mit kleiner Aufgabe bevorzugen

entries.source: This CLI version retains existing shared-storage access under Pod permissions. Future architecture should give each Pod its own state and one very small independently executable responsibility; storage replacement is a separate proposal.
entries.text: Diese CLI-Version erhält bestehenden gemeinsamen Speicherzugriff unter den Pod-Berechtigungen. Die künftige Architektur soll jedem Pod eigenen Zustand und eine sehr kleine eigenständig ausführbare Aufgabe geben; der Speicheraustausch ist ein eigener Vorschlag.

entries.source: Revision 4 adds explicit shared-domain-data and work access with Pod-scoped authorization. Records the owner direction of small independent Pods with Pod-owned state, while keeping storage replacement outside this implementation.
entries.text: Revision 4 ergänzt ausdrücklichen Zugriff auf gemeinsame Domain-Daten und Work mit Pod-bezogenen Berechtigungen. Die Richtung des Eigentümers zu kleinen eigenständigen Pods mit Pod-eigenem Zustand festgehalten; der Speicheraustausch bleibt außerhalb dieser Umsetzung.

entries.source: Patrick approved revision 4 in the chat: "Passt. Setze das cli um". Started implementation from current canonical main; no owner Pod has been modified.
entries.text: Patrick hat Revision 4 im Chat freigegeben: "Passt. Setze das cli um". Umsetzung aus aktuellem kanonischem main begonnen; kein Eigentümer-Pod wurde verändert.

entries.source: Revision 5 records the owner instruction to keep the CLI standalone for now. Removed desktop attachment and upgrade coordination; require desktop closed and share an OS lease between CLI workers.
entries.text: Revision 5 hält die Anweisung des Eigentümers fest, die CLI vorerst eigenständig zu halten. Desktop-Anbindung und Update-Abstimmung entfernt; Desktop muss geschlossen bleiben, CLI-Worker teilen eine Betriebssystem-Sperre.

approval.reference: User, after reviewing proposal revision 4: "Passt. Setze das cli um".
approval.scope: Implement the four CLI commands against the real database with existing Pod identity, configured home context and shared-data access; no additional application-secret management or storage migration.
